chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: The seven-piece band at the Casbah
summary: At the Casbah Lee led a seven-piece band with Maxwell Davis, Marshall Royal and others that played big-band arrangements and Dizzy's Manteca.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I still had my bands, and I started working out on
[Figaro4] I was trying to think of the name of the club. The Casbah.

The Casbah, that's the name of it, right -- out on Figaro4. Well, with the Casbah, let's see ... I think that was the band where I had -- this was when Les Brown and his band used to come to hear my band play, because we were playing things like "I Got My Love to Keep Me Warm", you know, that hit thing they had, and we were playing Dizzy's "Manteca" and I think at this time, it seems to me that I had John Simmons, Gerald Wiggins, Maxwell Davis, and Marshall Royal was playing in this band with me. And Henry Coker was playing trombone.

And we would play all the big band arrangements, and so all the bands would come and hear us, because I was a stickler for 7 pieces, because you could always get the big band sound out of 7 pieces, if it's voiced correctly.

Let's see ... Sarah Vaughn worked out there with us; that's when Black Coffee came out -- now whatever year "Black Coffee" was very popular, that's when I was there. That's when she was doing "Black Coffee".
